text:
micah: Heads up — Sequoia 40B is scheduled GA next Tuesday, EU + APAC first rollout. Ops wants a quick surge plan and rollback/fallback strategy. Who can own numbers?

kara: Did a light sim this morning. If traffic shape matches beta: EU peak tokens/sec goes from ~180k -> ~420k (2.33x). APAC peak from ~120k -> ~290k. Back-of-envelope extra GPU-hours: ~9.6k/week combined if we keep current batching. :grimacing:

samir: Oof. Main concerns: KV cache eviction will spike since median prompt length is up 1.4x. That kills warm-start gains. We'll need to increase per-shard memory or reduce max concurrent contexts. Also shard hotness will concentrate on eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1.

elaine: Network note — our peering to cloud-eu has a soft egress cap at 22 Gbps during business hours. At +2.3x token/s we hit that unless we throttle streaming chunk sizes or enable chunked compression. Talked to net; they can bump to 40 Gbps but it needs ticket and cost approval.

micah: Action items: 1) Simulate realistic conv/QPS on infra cluster (owner: kara). 2) Setup region-level fallback routing to quantized 8B (owner: samir). 3) Cost estimate for temporary peering bump (owner: elaine). 4) Canary plan + kill-switch (owner: eng release).

kara: Simulation snippet I used (feel free to reuse):
```bash
# sim load for sequoia 40b, 5m warmup, 20m window
./tools/simulate_tokens --model sequoia-40b --qps 1200 --concurrency 150 --mean_tokens 220 --duration 1500
```
Outputs: avg p95 latency jump from 42ms -> 130ms on a single A100-equivalent pool under current autoscaler thresholds. Batch sizes grow which increases tail latency.

samir: For fallback, thinking: route policy: prefer primary sequoia-40b (cost tier 2) -> fallback sequoia-8b-quant (tier 0.4) if queueing time >150ms or GPU backlog > 40%. Also add per-route cache warming for top 500 prompts to reduce cold KV misses.

elaine: Peering cost: provisional increase to 40 Gbps ~ $6k/month extra for EU region plus one-off change request. If we do on-demand scale via alternate region routing (send some EU traffic to us-west with lower peering cost) latency impact might be +30-50ms for some users. Need product sign-off.

micah: Can we avoid long-term capacity commits? Preferred: transient Dedicated nodes for first 72h of GA (spot-on-reserved mix) then measure sustained lift. Estimate: need extra 12 A100-equivalent GPUs in EU and 8 in APAC for first 72h to hit 95th percentile SLOs. That maps to ~2,160 GPU-hours (72h * 30 GPUs) across regions.

ops-bot: deploy-bot scheduled canary for sequoia-40b in eu-west-1 at 2024-07-12T08:00Z. Canary config: 5% traffic, TTL 30m, auto-rollback on error-rate >1.2% or latency >200ms.

kara: I'll run a long sim overnight with updated token distribution and attach dashboard screenshots in the morning. If numbers hold, recommend pre-warm: 1) spin up quantized variants in same AZs, 2) pre-load top-200 prompt cache, 3) set autoscaler cool-down to 90s.

samir: I'll prep fallback routing rules and a small admission controller that drops to 8B for single-request token counts >2k to protect KV cache. Will post PR for review by EOD.

elaine: Opening peering ticket now, cc @finance for short-term approval. If finance pushes back, contingency is soft-sharding traffic to us-west and applying a region-weight cap.

micah: Thanks — this is the kind of quick coordination we needed. Please post sim artifacts and cost delta by EOD today. If anyone sees a different pattern, flag it here. :thumbsup:
